newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar dives as March premium paces NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar dives as March premium paces NY.

text.p: London's March white sugar contract slumped to psychological support at $300 per tonne as the market's white premium scrambled to keep pace with a fierce bout of selling in the raws market, traders said on Tuesday. Commission house and broker selling accounted for the bulk of the March volume, which was mainly composed of outright dealings, they said.
"It seems to be premium selling...New York has gone all the way down and the premium hasn't widened at all," said one. "There just seems to be a glut of selling there."

The March white/raw premium opened at around $69.50 and then widened to $71. Mixed buyers at the lows prevented the spot position from falling under $300 and by 1612 GMT it stood $4.00 lower at $300.70.
May was down $3.90 at $300.50 and volume totalled a solid 2,495 lots. New York's equivalent March contract tumbled 30 points to an intraday low of 10.36 cents/lb.
March last dipped below $300.00 on November 22, when values slipped back inside a major downtrend channel in place since the middle of September.
Earlier in the session, one trade house dominated the thin activity as both a buyer and seller of March, with scattered commission house crosses boosting the overall volume.
The spot contract in Paris also lost ground, possibly on account of pre-hedging against Wednesday's European Union tender for sugar export licences.
March was down $3.60 at $301.00 and May down $1.60 at $303.00. Matif volume was light at 323 lots.
